objective: Implement a safe WhatsApp notification layer for the existing MYTHOS GitHub Bridge. When a task reaches a terminal report state, the Bridge must send a single WhatsApp notification through a provider adapter. This task is ONLY for Bridge notifications and must not implement MYTHOS AUTO WhatsApp functionality.
scope: Inspect the existing GitHub Bridge and integrate a notification adapter without changing its execution semantics.
Evaluate the previously identified self-hosted projects Evolution API, WAHA, MultiWA and WaSphere and select the safest appropriate provider for this narrow notification use case.
Prefer Evolution API if inspection confirms it is the best fit, but do not assume the choice without evaluation.
Keep the provider behind an adapter so a future migration to official WhatsApp Business Cloud API does not require rewriting the Bridge.
Send notifications for COMPLETED, FAILED, BLOCKED and HUMAN_APPROVAL only.
Implement durable idempotency so repeated Bridge polling, restart or concurrent ticks cannot duplicate successful notifications.
Ensure WhatsApp failure never changes the actual GitHub task/report status or breaks the Bridge.
Use secure environment/secret configuration and never commit or log WhatsApp credentials.
Add automated tests using mocks and perform one controlled real smoke test only after all automated tests pass.
Integrate safely with the existing Bridge service/timer and document configuration, security, retry and rollback behavior.
constraints: Do NOT implement MYTHOS AUTO WhatsApp/customer-chat functionality; this task is only the first Bridge notification layer.
Do NOT rebuild or redesign MCP, ContextForge, OTHMODE or the existing AI Executor.
Do NOT touch AUTOS-0, SPY, n8n or unrelated projects.
Do NOT change protected governance policy or bypass the existing governance relay.
Do NOT expose, commit or print API keys, access tokens, passwords, QR/session credentials, authorization headers or other secrets.
Do NOT use blind git add .; stage only explicitly intended files.
Do NOT push directly with raw git push; use the existing MYTHOS governance relay.
Do NOT send real WhatsApp messages during automated tests.
WhatsApp must be disabled by default until explicitly configured and enabled.
Prefer private/local networking for the WhatsApp provider; do not expose it publicly unless strictly required.
Keep the deployment lightweight because the VPS has previously shown severe swap pressure.
Use the existing MYTHOS storage/configuration conventions where possible; do not add an unnecessary database.
Preserve existing green test suites and existing Bridge/OTHMODE/Executor semantics.
validation_requirements: Validate the provider choice and document why it is appropriate.
Test COMPLETED, FAILED, BLOCKED and HUMAN_APPROVAL notifications.
Verify PENDING and non-terminal states do not trigger notifications.
Verify duplicate polling and concurrent ticks result in at most one successful notification.
Verify failed delivery is retryable and does not alter task status.
Verify restart/recovery does not duplicate successful delivery.
Verify secrets are absent from Git, logs, reports and test output.
Run the relevant existing Bridge, OTHMODE, Executor and governance tests plus the new notification tests.
Perform one controlled real WhatsApp smoke test only after automated tests pass.
Verify deployment/restart recovery and create the normal GitHub REPORT with commit SHA, tests, risks and delivery status.
